impact_summary: Customers across AWS were affected by a disruption centered on the us-east-1 Region that began at 11:48 PM PDT on October 19 and ended at 2:20 PM PDT on October 20. DynamoDB API error rates were elevated from 11:48 PM to 2:40 AM, and DynamoDB global table replicas experienced prolonged replication lag to and from us-east-1. New EC2 instance launches failed from 2:25 AM to 10:36 AM, with some newly launched instances lacking connectivity until 1:50 PM, and Network Load Balancer experienced increased connection errors from 5:30 AM to 2:09 PM. Dependent services including Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, STS, IAM sign-in to the console, Amazon Connect, and Redshift were also impaired for periods ranging from roughly two hours to over a day.

action_items.action: Fix the DNS Enactor race condition by enforcing that a plan can only be applied if it is newer than the currently active plan, verified atomically at the time of the Route53 transaction rather than with a one-time check before apply begins

Change the plan clean-up process so it never deletes the currently active plan or any plan that a delayed Enactor could still apply, and add a guard that refuses to leave an endpoint with an empty DNS record

Add automated detection and repair for empty or missing DNS records on DynamoDB regional endpoints, with alerting that pages on-call when the active plan is absent and the Enactors cannot make progress

Document and rehearse a runbook for recovering DynamoDB DNS state manually, including how to restore the active plan and resume Enactor operation, so recovery does not depend on ad hoc operator decisions
Reduce dependency of EC2 DWFM state checks on DynamoDB, or provide a cached or degraded-mode lease mechanism so existing droplet leases are not lost during a DynamoDB outage
Create a documented, tested procedure for re-establishing DWFM leases across the fleet after a large-scale lease loss, including staged throttling, queue-drain limits, and controlled host restarts
Make the NLB health check subsystem wait for Network Manager propagation confirmation before bringing newly launched EC2 instances into service
Add rate limiting or circuit breaking to automatic AZ DNS failover in NLB so that a degraded health check subsystem cannot remove multi-AZ capacity from service
Add monitoring for Network Manager propagation backlog and for oscillating NLB health check results, with alerts that fire before capacity is removed from service

Ensure Lambda's SQS-polling subsystem and instance scaling recover automatically after upstream dependency failures, and prevent health-check-driven instance termination from under-scaling the fleet during recovery
Remove the dependency of Redshift IAM user credential resolution on an IAM API endpoint in us-east-1 so that cross-Region query paths do not fail due to a single-Region outage
Remove the dependency of AWS Management Console sign-in and STS on DynamoDB and NLB in us-east-1, or provide a regional fallback path for IAM authentication
Fix the AWS Support Center account metadata subsystem so that a regional failover returns valid responses rather than blocking legitimate users
Review DNS TTL settings for DynamoDB endpoints and document expected client-visible recovery time, so customers can plan for cached record expiry after a DNS incident
Improve incident triage by adding a runbook entry and dashboard panel that surfaces DynamoDB DNS state as a first check when multiple services report DynamoDB connection failures simultaneously
